title: What time is it?
title_target: ម៉ោងប៉ុន្មានហើយ — maong pon-maan haeuy
goal: Read and tell the time — and know exactly where the half hour belongs: កន្លះ attaches to the hour that has ALREADY passed, just like English "half past".
bekal: ask and answer ម៉ោងប៉ុន្មាន?
say "half past" with កន្លះ without being an hour off
give minutes with នាទី and ខ្វះ
divide the day into ព្រឹក, ថ្ងៃត្រង់, រសៀល, ល្ងាច, យប់
make an appointment with ម៉ោង … ជួបគ្នា

dialogs.title: កិច្ចសន្ទនា — Making a dinner date
dialogs.intro: Sreymom invites Ani to dinner with her family. In the fifth line, Ani — whose own language counts half hours toward the NEXT hour — makes exactly the mistake this unit is about, and Sreymom corrects her. Read that line twice.

grammars.title: ⚠️ កន្លះ attaches to the hour that has ALREADY passed
body: Get this wrong and the result is not an odd sentence but **an appointment missed by an hour**. The good news for English speakers: Khmer works like English "half past". It names the hour that **has already passed** and adds a half: "two and a half" = 2:30. The trap is for anyone who also speaks German, Dutch, or Indonesian, where "half three" means 2:30 — half an hour **toward** three.

head: Time
Khmer
Say it
Literally
rows: ម៉ោងពីរកន្លះ
ម៉ោងប្រាំពីរកន្លះ
ម៉ោងដប់ពីរកន្លះ

after: ⚠️ So ម៉ោងប្រាំពីរកន្លះ = **7:30 pm** (19:30), not 6:30. If you think "half past seven", you are right; if you think "half seven" the German way, you will arrive an hour early.
The safest way to avoid trouble: **don't translate at all**. Read ម៉ោងប្រាំពីរកន្លះ as "seven thirty" — the hour, then thirty. That way Khmer, English, and your digital watch all agree.
Hindi works the same way (साढ़े तीन = 3:30), and so does Burmese (ခွဲ). German, Dutch, and Indonesian are among the few languages that name the next hour instead.

grammars.title: Saying the minutes: នាទី and ខ្វះ
body: Apart from the half hour, minutes are given in two ways: by adding ("past") or by subtracting ("to").

head: Time
Khmer
Say it

ម៉ោងបី ដប់ប្រាំនាទី
ម៉ោងបីកន្លះ
ម៉ោងបួន ខ្វះដប់ប្រាំនាទី
ម៉ោងបួន ខ្វះដប់នាទី

after: ⚠️ Look at the rows for 3:45 and 3:50: with ខ្វះ ("lacking"), it is **the next hour** that gets named. ម៉ោងបួនខ្វះដប់នាទី is literally "four o'clock lacking ten minutes" — exactly the logic of English "ten to four". Everything here matches English habits.

grammars.title: Dividing up the day
body: Khmer divides the day into five parts, and the part is added **after** the hour to remove any doubt about morning or evening — much like English "a.m." and "p.m.", only with five slots.

head: Khmer
Say it
Roughly
Example
rows: ម៉ោងដប់ពីរថ្ងៃត្រង់ — 12:00

after: Cambodia uses the twelve-hour clock in everyday conversation and the twenty-four-hour clock in official schedules. Naming the part of the day is almost always necessary — ម៉ោងប្រាំពីរ on its own can mean morning or evening, and people will ask back ព្រឹកឬយប់?

blocks.title: Time and good manners in Cambodia
items: **Fifteen minutes late counts as on time** for personal meetings. For office matters and appointments with foreigners, punctuality is expected as usual.
**A dinner invitation usually means arriving early, not late.** A Cambodian host has been cooking since the afternoon, and a guest who arrives half an hour early is actually welcome.
⚠️ **Don't phone after nine in the evening** unless it is truly urgent. Many Cambodian families go to bed earlier than big-city people do, and get up before sunrise.
